title: The test engine's records
description: Draft for approval. The registry (what exists, generated and published like help.json), a run (what happened, kept under build/), a finding and its rule (what a check reported, in the shape of SARIF). A test's id is derived, never declared.

id.description: kind:path::name for unit, python and js (the file and the test's own name), kind:name for a scenario (its file stem) and a check (its script), and scenario:name#step for one scenario step. Derived from the test, so a rename is a new test and git is its history.

subject.description: What a test is about: a module type as help.json names it, or a class or script where it is not a type. Links to the help and MoonWalk exist where the subject is a type.

size.description: Google's test sizes: small in one process, medium on the desktop with a server, large on hardware or a network.

title.description: A unit test's sentence, a scenario's name, a check's one line.

file.description: The path of the test, relative to the repository.

subjects.description: From a unit test's @module and @also, and a scenario's module and also.

controls.description: Type.control, from a scenario's set_control and expect_control steps through its declared instances.

steps.description: process/step ids the test proves, named in the test (a steps_proved key, a @step tag); the generator checks they exist.

sequence.description: A scenario's own steps in order: what it does and what each step is for. They are not process steps.

perf.description: A measured step's numbers per target: the contract it is held to and the range it was observed in. The samples stay out; step 7 of the plan moves the observations into the run record.

run.description: The MoonDeck call that runs it.
One run of one test, kept under build/ and never committed. JUnit XML is read into it where a runner writes it.

tree.description: The git tree id the run saw, as walk_status records it: a pass counts while the files it covers are unchanged.

measurement.description: A scenario's observation: what was measured on which target. Not pass or fail. The contract it is compared against stays committed beside the scenario, as a golden file does.

rule.description: In the shape of SARIF's reportingDescriptor: the rule, its reason and its page, so the standards pages generate from the rules.

standard.description: The standards page and anchor that holds the rule.

finding.description: In the shape of a SARIF result.

description: The registry: every test by its id.
